correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3, the normalized cut vertices have exact Frobenius Gram G=(1/2)diag(w)^(-1)Kdiag(w)^(-1); the discrete Dirichlet Green identity K^(-1)=L/n and Lw=2 determine all affine facet gradients. Their reciprocal-height weights give the unique incenter and exact r^2. Solving 2Gmu-diag(G)=kappa*1 gives strictly positive circumcenter barycentric weights, proving unique minimum enclosing radius via a weighted variance identity. det(K)=n^(n-2) and a simplex Gram determinant give volume. Independently assembled standard-library rational matrices reproduce all exact identities for n=3..10. The finite tests are not extrapolated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The face is a natural canonical model of all normalized nonnegative line metrics within the Monge cost simplex. The theorem completely determines its intrinsic Euclidean optimal interior and exterior approximating balls and exact dimensional volume for every n. The incenter is unexpectedly the equally spaced path metric, while the enclosing center adds strong terminal-cut weight; every vertex is an extremal contact. The aspect ratio grows as n^2/6 despite fixed simplex combinatorics. These exact non-obvious identities are useful quantitative benchmarks for metric-cost polyhedral geometry and are not known-table recomputations.
